NDT training in Salt Lake City: how it works for Salt Lake City employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Salt Lake City and Wasatch Front employers and technicians in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I, II and III. Theory runs live online, and practical training runs onsite at your facility, from Ogden to Magna to Provo, under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification is issued by your employer under its written practice once you have completed classroom training, documented experience, the exams and a vision test.

Salt Lake City has one of the most unusual NDT markets in the country. In a single metro area you find five petroleum refineries, one of the largest US Air Force maintenance depots, the solid-rocket-motor industry, commercial aerostructures, a major copper mine and smelter, and interstate pipelines. Those sectors do not all qualify NDT personnel the same way. Refineries work to SNT-TC-1A with API credentials for the inspectors of record. Aerospace works to NAS 410 with Nadcap-accredited processes. Military depots work to Air Force technical orders. Rocket-motor inspection uses techniques, radiography and computed tomography in particular, at scales rarely seen elsewhere. A technician who understands which system an employer runs, and which one they are training for, has a real advantage on the Wasatch Front.

Most people searching for NDT training in Salt Lake City fall into one of a few groups. Some are new hires at refinery-service or fabrication contractors who need Level I and II quickly. Some are technicians leaving military service at Hill Air Force Base who have NDT skills and want a civilian SNT-TC-1A certification. Some are manufacturing employees at aerospace and defence suppliers adding a method. And some are small shops that have won work from a prime contractor and need a documented NDT programme to keep it. Atlantis NDT supports all of them with formal method training, exam preparation and Level III services. The certification itself is always issued by the employer.

Our scope is also clear. Atlantis NDT trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Salt Lake City employers may also ask for NAS 410 aerospace qualification, API 510, 570 or 653 inspector certification, or AWS CWI. Those are separate schemes, and we do not train or certify to them. SNT-TC-1A method training gives technicians the knowledge base those schemes rely on. And for refinery and industrial employers, SNT-TC-1A is the personnel scheme itself. Ask us which scheme fits the job you are targeting.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Salt Lake City

Every method below is available to Salt Lake City employers and technicians as live-virtual classroom theory, onsite cohorts at your facility, or a blend. Content follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge and the employer's written practice, with practical work on real specimens. Required hours depend on method, level and written practice. See the training requirements matrix for recommended figures.

MethodLevelsWhat Salt Lake City employers use it forPrerequisite

Level II: Level I experience per the written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, II (Level III through UT)Encoded weld inspection in fabrication and refinery turnarounds, corrosion mapping on refinery piping and vessels, and composite inspection in aerostructuresUT Level II strongly recommended
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, II (Level III through UT)Thick-wall pressure vessel welds and crack sizing during refinery turnarounds and new vessel fabricationUT Level II strongly recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, IIIPipe weld radiography in refineries and pipelines, casting and weld radiography in aerospace and defence manufacturing, and large-scale radiography of rocket-motor componentsRadiation-safety training and state requirements for radiographers and assistants, plus RT method training
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, IIICarbon-steel weld inspection, landing-gear and steel component inspection in aircraft maintenance, and crack detection on mining equipment and structural steelMethod training and a vision test

The Salt Lake City method mix splits along sector lines. On the refinery side, north of downtown along the I-15 corridor through North Salt Lake and Woods Cross, UT thickness, PAUT corrosion mapping, RT and MT dominate. On the aerospace and defence side, from Hill Air Force Base and Ogden down to the manufacturing plants west of the city, ET, PT and UT dominate, with MT on landing gear and steel parts. Technicians who can work both sides by holding UT plus ET, or UT plus PT, are unusually versatile in this market.

For technicians preparing for Level III, Atlantis NDT runs ASNT Level III exam preparation covering the Basic exam and method exams, delivered online.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Salt Lake City, step by step

  1. Your employer's written practice. The written practice defines how the employer trains, examines and certifies NDT personnel: hours, exams, grading, vision requirements, recertification and the responsible Level III. No written practice means no SNT-TC-1A certification. See written-practice development.
  2. Formal classroom training. Method training delivered live-virtual, onsite or blended, to the hours in the written practice. Recommended figures are in the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised experience in the method on real work, logged and signed. Refinery turnarounds can build experience hours quickly because of the sheer volume of examinations. Aerospace production work builds them steadily.
  4. General examination. A written exam on the principles of the method.
  5. Specific examination. A written exam on the employer's procedures, codes and equipment, for example refinery inspection procedures and ASME B31.3 acceptance criteria, or a customer's aerospace process specification.
  6. Practical examination. A hands-on exam on real specimens with real discontinuities, administered and graded by a Level III or designated examiner.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast testing per the written practice, repeated annually.
  8. Certification by the employer. The employer certifies you for the method and level, and the records are kept on file for audit.
  9. Recertification. On the interval set by the written practice. Certification generally ends when you leave an employer, and a new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice, often crediting documented prior training and experience.

For veterans coming out of military NDT roles at Hill Air Force Base or elsewhere, military training and experience can be valuable evidence, but they do not convert automatically into civilian SNT-TC-1A certification. The civilian employer's Level III decides what credit to give under the written practice. Usually some formal training and the full set of exams are still required. Our SNT-TC-1A guide covers this in more detail.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Salt Lake City crews

Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in Salt Lake City or anywhere else. Training reaches Wasatch Front employers in three ways.

Live-virtual classroom. Instructor-led theory online, with questions, exercises and quizzes in real time. This works well for technicians spread from Ogden to Provo, because nobody has to drive the length of the valley in winter traffic to sit in a classroom. See online NDT training.

Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-led instructor comes to your facility for practical training and practical exams, bringing reference specimens or using your own. For defence manufacturers with controlled access, you arrange instructor access or provide a training room outside controlled areas.

Blended. Theory online, practical onsite. This is the common choice for Salt Lake City employers training several people at once.

Timing matters on the Wasatch Front. Refinery turnarounds absorb every available technician for weeks at a time and are usually planned for spring and autumn. Aerospace production schedules run steadily but tightly. Mountain winters slow some outdoor pipeline and construction work, which can open a window for training. We schedule cohorts around those cycles, not against them. Ask about onsite training for your Salt Lake City crew, and we will send cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Multi-site or multi-method programmes run through our corporate NDT training service.

Where NDT technicians work in Salt Lake City

The refinery corridor. Utah has five petroleum refineries, clustered north of Salt Lake City in North Salt Lake and Woods Cross. They include Marathon's Salt Lake City refinery (the largest in the state, operating since 1908), Chevron's Salt Lake refinery, HF Sinclair's Woods Cross refinery, Big West Oil's North Salt Lake refinery and a smaller independent refinery in Woods Cross. Together they supply most of the gasoline and diesel used in Utah and Idaho. Refinery inspection runs on SNT-TC-1A for NDT personnel, with API 510, 570 and 653 inspectors of record responsible for vessels, piping and tanks. Codes such as ASME B31.3, ASME Section VIII and API 650/653 govern what technicians inspect. Turnarounds are the busiest periods for NDT contractors in the region. The refineries also illustrate a local risk: the March 2020 Magna earthquake reminded operators that seismic events can trigger unplanned inspection of equipment, supports and piping.

Hill Air Force Base and the Ogden Air Logistics Complex. North of Salt Lake City, the Ogden Air Logistics Complex at Hill AFB is one of the Air Force's major depots, maintaining front-line aircraft including the F-35 and F-16, and handling landing gear for a wide range of Air Force aircraft. Depot NDT is heavy on ET, UT, PT and MT for aircraft structures, components and landing gear. Air Force NDT follows Technical Order 33B-1-1 and related technical orders, and civilian personnel qualification in this area references NAS 410. Contractors and suppliers supporting depot work need to know which system applies to their scope.

Rocket motors and defence manufacturing. Northern Utah is the centre of the US solid-rocket-motor industry. Northrop Grumman's Promontory operations build large solid rocket motors and boosters, and its Magna site produces motors and composite structures. Northrop Grumman's Roy campus is the headquarters of the Sentinel ICBM programme. Inspection here involves radiography and computed tomography of motor cases and propellant, UT and bond inspection of composite cases, and precision NDT on metallic hardware, all under strict defence quality requirements. L3Harris and a network of defence suppliers along the Wasatch Front add further scope.

Commercial aerostructures. Boeing's Salt Lake City plant builds composite structures for commercial aircraft, including 787 tail components. Composite aerostructures rely heavily on automated and manual UT for porosity, delamination and bond-line inspection. Aerospace suppliers in the region work under NAS 410 personnel qualification and Nadcap-accredited NDT processes. SNT-TC-1A method knowledge is directly relevant, but the certification scheme is different.

Mining, smelting and heavy industry. Rio Tinto's Kennecott Utah Copper operates the Bingham Canyon mine southwest of the city, along with the smelter and refinery near Magna. Heavy mining equipment, haul-truck frames, crushers, conveyors and smelter vessels need UT, MT and VT on structural welds and wear components, and thickness surveys on process vessels and piping.

Pipelines and energy. Interstate gas transmission pipelines such as Kern River run through Utah. Crude and product pipelines feed the refineries and carry fuel to neighbouring states. The regional gas utility, now part of Enbridge, maintains distribution and transmission lines across the state. Pipeline weld inspection follows API 1104, and pipeline operators require operator qualification for covered tasks. That is a separate federal requirement from NDT method certification. Power generation, including the Intermountain Power Project near Delta, which is converting to natural gas and hydrogen-capable units, adds boiler, piping and heat-exchanger inspection.

Radiography licensing. Utah is an NRC Agreement State, and has been since 1984. The Utah Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control, within the Department of Environmental Quality, licenses radioactive-material use, including sealed-source industrial radiography, and registers x-ray equipment. The state's industrial radiography rules follow the federal Part 34 model, requiring approved training programmes and recognised radiation-safety qualification for radiographers on top of SNT-TC-1A RT certification. RT crews coming from other states should confirm reciprocity with the licensee before mobilising. For salary context, see our NDT salary guide. We do not publish local salary figures here.

Level III services and written practices for Salt Lake City NDT companies

The Wasatch Front has a dense supply chain of small and mid-sized fabricators, machine shops and service companies that feed the refineries, the depot and the defence primes. Many of them reach the same point: a customer audit asks for their NDT written practice, their Level III and their certification records, and what they have does not hold up. Atlantis NDT helps with:

  • Written practices that fit what the company actually does, with the right methods, levels and customer requirements, and no copied-in obligations it cannot meet. See written-practice development.
  • Outside Level III services, covering procedure approval, exam administration and grading, and certification sign-off. This is normal and allowed under SNT-TC-1A for companies that do not need a full-time Level III.
  • Procedures and technique sheets for refinery corrosion mapping, pipeline weld UT, composite inspection and other specialised techniques.
  • Programme audits before a customer or prime contractor visits, so gaps are found internally first.

Details are on the SNT-TC-1A guidance page. Book a Level III consultation to scope a written practice, prepare for an audit or take over a programme that has drifted.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical exams test process as much as knowledge: set-up, calibration, coverage, indication evaluation and documentation. Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Salt Lake City, that covers both sides of the market. The aircraft hangar environment suits depot and aerospace technicians, and the oil and gas site and storage tank environments suit refinery work.

The simulator is for practice only. It does not replace the practical examination, which under SNT-TC-1A must be done on real specimens with real discontinuities using actual equipment, graded by a Level III or designated examiner. For the written exams, try our UT Level 2 practice questions and similar mock exams.

Your instructor

Atlantis NDT training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop sets the course content, oversees onsite and live-virtual delivery, and provides Level III oversight for employers who use Atlantis NDT's Level III services. See the full NDT training catalogue.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Salt Lake City

How do I get NDT certified in Salt Lake City?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete formal method training, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass a vision test. Aerospace employers may qualify you under NAS 410 instead, and refinery inspectors of record also need API certification. Both are separate from SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Can I take NDT training online in Utah?

Yes. Method theory runs as live-virtual classroom sessions you can join from anywhere in Utah. The practical portion and practical exam need hands-on work with real specimens, and Atlantis NDT delivers that onsite at your employer's facility.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the classroom hours in your employer's written practice, the on-the-job experience you must log and your exam schedule. The classroom portion is quick. Experience hours take longest, though a busy turnaround season can speed them up. See the training requirements matrix for recommended figures.

Do I need a license for radiography in Utah?

The license is held by the company. Companies doing industrial radiography with radioactive sources in Utah need a license from the Utah Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control, and x-ray equipment must be registered. Individual radiographers need recognised radiation-safety qualification and training under the licensee's programme, in addition to SNT-TC-1A RT certification.

What does NDT training cost in Salt Lake City?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on method, level, group size, onsite versus online delivery and any Level III services needed. Cohort and onsite quotes are sent within one business day. Request a Salt Lake City training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Salt Lake City employers?

Yes, especially in refining, pipelines, fabrication, mining and industrial services, where SNT-TC-1A is the standard personnel framework. Aerospace and depot work often uses NAS 410 and Air Force technical orders, which draw on the same method knowledge but have their own qualification rules. Because SNT-TC-1A is employer-based, a new employer re-certifies you under its written practice.

I did NDT in the Air Force. Can I get a civilian certification?

Your military training and experience are valuable, but they do not convert automatically. A civilian employer's Level III decides how much documented training and experience to credit under its written practice, and you will usually still sit the general, specific and practical exams. Atlantis NDT can provide formal training to fill gaps and exam preparation to help the transition.

Which methods are most in demand along the Wasatch Front?

UT is valuable across both refining and aerospace. On the refinery side, PAUT corrosion mapping, RT and MT are in steady demand. On the aerospace and depot side, ET and PT are core methods. Technicians holding UT plus ET or UT plus PT can work in both sectors.

Do refinery NDT technicians in Salt Lake City need API certification?

NDT technicians performing the examinations are usually certified under SNT-TC-1A. API 510, 570 and 653 certifications are for the inspectors of record who take responsibility for pressure vessels, piping and tanks. Atlantis NDT does not train for API certifications. Some technicians later pursue them as a career step.

Can you train our crew at our facility in Ogden or West Valley City?

Yes. Onsite cohorts run at your facility anywhere along the Wasatch Front, with theory delivered online first so onsite days are spent on practical work. For controlled-access defence sites, you arrange instructor access or provide a room outside controlled areas.

Our shop needs an NDT programme for a new defence contract. Where do we start?

Start with a written practice and a responsible Level III, then train and certify your people under that programme. Atlantis NDT can provide all three and, if your customer requires NAS 410, advise on how that differs. Book a Level III consultation.

Do you offer Level III exam preparation in Salt Lake City?

Yes. Our ASNT Level III exam preparation covers the Basic exam and method exams and is delivered live online, so Utah candidates can prepare without travelling.
